events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph first.** I'd expect pier salmon fishing this week to be about **1 (below average)**. The pier has no salmon reports in this period, so treat this as an estimate.
- **South Haven is the backup,** also about **1**, with the same caveat.
- **Grand Haven: 1.** Its only pier report is from late May and was slow.
- **Muskegon: 0 to 1.** Its newest report is 41 days old and its latest boat report was slow.
- If the pier is slow, the reports suggest that boats fishing 100+ feet of water, with spoons, do better. That is a boat plan, not a pier plan.

## Why

- **No recent pier salmon reports exist for these four ports.** The only pier salmon reports are Grand Haven from May 24 (slow) and May 31 (a few fish on alewives), so the ratings above are my estimate from boat results.
- **Water is warm.** Today's buoy readings are about 68 to 71 F, and I'd expect salmon to sit deeper than the pier can reach, since the reference puts Chinook at 52-58 F.
- **Recent boat results are average at best.** The July 5 St. Joseph boat report was average (2) and South Haven's was below average (1), both with fish deep.
- **Similar past weeks were mostly slow.** In past seasons with about 70 F surface water, most boat reports were slow or below average.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is 13 days old for St. Joseph and South Haven; 27 days for Grand Haven; 41 days for Muskegon)**
- St. Joseph (2023-07-05): boats had "decent fishing," quality 2, "well beyond 120 feet of water." No pier report.
- South Haven (2023-07-05): fair, quality 1, fish "around 100 feet," mostly on spoons.
- Grand Haven (2023-06-21): boats quality 2 in 65-160 feet of water, fish 35-90 feet down, orange spoons and meat rigs.
- Grand Haven (2023-05-24, pier): slow (quality 0), "a few were caught on alewives."
- Muskegon (2023-06-07): boats slow; a few Chinook 30-100 feet down.

**Past seasons (similar water, about 70 F)**
- Most boat reports were slow or below average: Grand Haven (2022-07-14, quality 0), Muskegon (2022-07-14, quality 0), South Haven (2022-07-06, quality 0), and St. Joseph (2022-07-06, quality 1, "very spotty").
- The St. Joseph (2022-07-06) report said the best water was 30-40 feet deep, but those fish were on flies and Spin Doctors, not from a pier.

**Conditions now**
- The buoy surface readings for the week before today were about 68 F (Grand Haven, Muskegon) and 71 F (St. Joseph, South Haven). St. Joseph was flat over the week (-0 F), so I see no sign of upwelling there.
- No modeled pierhead temperature came back, so I can't give pier water temperature.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are 13 to 41 days old, and the conditions data is a summary for the week before today, not live readings.
- The pier ratings are my estimate. The reports say nothing about pier salmon this summer.
- The cold-layer depth wasn't returned, so I can't give a modeled depth for the fish.
- The reference notes that a sharp drop in buoy temperature (upwelling) is what brings salmon to piers. If you see that, St. Joseph or South Haven may improve. Check before you go.

## Sources

- St. Joseph & South Haven, July 5: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven & South Haven, June 21: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Grand Haven & Muskegon, June 7: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35ed629
- Grand Haven (pier), May 24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35c6304
- Grand Haven (pier), May 31: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35d8a8c
- Past seasons, July 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a
